preamble: Affrication of the palatal stop [c] to the postalveolar affricate [tʃ] adds a fricated release and moves the closure slightly forward. It is the usual second step in velar palatalization chains (k > c > tʃ), and it is observed directly where [c] exists. Standard Modern Greek realizes /k/ as [c] before front vowels, and southern dialects carry this further to an affricate, giving [tʃe] for standard [ce] 'and'; palato-alveolar outcomes are reported for Cyprus, alveolo-palatal [tɕ] for Crete. In Albanian the palatal stop q /c/ merges with ç /tʃ/ for many speakers, especially in Northern Gheg, where q in qen 'dog' is realized as [t͡ʃ].

examples.from: και 'and', standard [ce] (conservative pronunciation with [c] before e)
examples.note: The from-form is the conservative pronunciation kept in Standard Modern Greek; the southern dialects push the palatal stop on to an affricate.

examples.from: Κυριακή /kiriaˈki/ 'Sunday', with [c] before i in Standard Modern Greek
examples.note: Area of palatalisation of /k/ to [tʃ]; the Cycladic tsitakism area has [tsirjaˈtsi] instead.
